title: Cold rebuild: storage that survives the pod
summary: Move a Deployment to a PersistentVolumeClaim on a real Kubernetes cluster, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *volumes and persistence* you moved a Deployment's data from an `emptyDir` to a
PersistentVolumeClaim on a real cluster and proved it survives the pod. Now do it again from memory: the same
scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Your app writes uploaded images to `/app/uploads` inside the container, with no volume. The pod is rescheduled after a node upgrade. What happens to the images?
options: They are gone: they were in the container's writable layer on the old node
They are copied to the new node by the kubelet
steps.explain: Use a PersistentVolumeClaim, or better for uploads, object storage (Blob Storage, S3) so any replica can read them.

steps.title: Storage that survives the pod, cold
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`).
Switch the `notes` Deployment from its `emptyDir` to a 256Mi PersistentVolumeClaim `notes-data` mounted at `/data`,
write the notes `buy milk` and `ship v2` into `/data/notes.txt`, replace the pod, and make sure the new pod has them.
From memory: no hints this time.
